subject: Post-demo: deployment decision matrix + commit ask
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jocelyn Park <jocelyn@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: deployment decision matrix + commit ask

Thanks again for your time this morning, Jocelyn — appreciate the candid signal on latency targets and privacy constraints. Quick recap plus asks so we can get a compact pricing/ops proposal to your procurement team: 

- Summary of what we heard: peak inference ~250 concurrent requests during flash sales, typical QPS ~40, 95th p90 latency target ~120ms for product search reranks, and requirement that PII never leave Atlas VPC for logged sessions.
- Deployment options you flagged: Hosted API (fastest to production), Dedicated Reserved (predictable throughput, single-tenant GPU), Private VPC/on-prem (required for some regulated data flows).

What we need from you to finalize numbers: 
1) Confirmation of expected 30/60/90 day peak QPS distribution (quick table is fine).
2) Procurement timeline and preferred commercial model: per-token (hosted) vs reserved commit (dedicated) vs license + infra (private).
3) Any minimum security questionnaire fields we should prioritize (SOC3? custom encryption keys?).

I've attached a deployment decision matrix (redwood_deployment_matrix_v2.pdf) and a rough pricing workbook (pricing_estimate_draft.xlsx) with worked examples for each mode. Next steps I propose: we prepare two artifacts by Wednesday — a 1-pager recommendation and a formal quote for the model config you leaned toward on the call.

If you prefer, we can loop in Samir from procurement to review cadence/PO terms.

Thanks — laura

--
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_deployment_matrix_v2.pdf)
(Attachment: pricing_estimate_draft.xlsx)
From: Jocelyn Park <jocelyn@atlasretail.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.g@atlasretail.com>, security@atlasretail.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment decision matrix + commit ask

Thanks Laura — great summary. A few clarifications and data points from our side: 

- QPS profile (approx): baseline 30 QPS, promotional spikes up to ~260 QPS for 5-8 minute windows, average daily 12k requests.
- Latency: p95 must be <= 200ms; p90 target 120ms is accurate.
- Privacy: session logs may contain hashed identifiers; anything that can be re-identified must be disabled or locked to our KMS. This is a hard requirement for production.

Commercial preference: we'd like a price comparison. Our procurement team prefers reserved capacity for predictable cost, but they want a clear per-token equivalent so we can compare to other vendors. Also please include an example first-year commit (monthly GPU pools) and an on-demand overflow rate for bursts.

Procurement timeline: Samir will review and expects to issue an RFP shortlist by May 1. He may ask for an executed NDA and a standard SOW template.

Looping Samir and security. Jocelyn
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jocelyn Park <jocelyn@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment decision matrix + commit ask

Hi Jocelyn — quick pricing note and worked example to make the comparison apples-to-apples. High-level:

1) Hosted API (per-token):
- Unit: per input+output token.
- Example: For your avg request size (estimated 350 tokens total) at 12k/day => ~4.2M tokens/day.
- Monthly run-rate example: at hosted X cents/token => $YYk/mo (see attached workbook for exact formulas).

2) Dedicated Reserved (capacity):
- Unit: reserved GPU-hours / pool sizing with commit discount.
- Example: A 4-GPU pool (A100 equivalent) with autoscale for burst capacity + on-demand overflow. Committed rate reduces effective per-token cost by ~35-45% depending on utilization. We modeled three utilization scenarios (60/75/90%).

3) Private VPC / On-prem:
- Unit: license + infra + ops. Upfront uplift for setup and integrations; good long-term if you need full data residency and constant heavy utilization.

Attachment: quote-Atlas-20270412.pdf includes a worked 12-month commit showing monthly cost vs hosted per-token baseline and an overflow pricing table.

Recommendation: For Atlas' profile (flash spikes + strict KMS requirement) a hybrid Dedicated Reserved with configured overflow to Hosted API is usually the lowest friction. It gives predictable unit economics for baseline traffic and a safety valve for the spikes without long procurement cycles.

If helpful, we can produce a short sensitivity table showing break-even utilization rates for the 4-GPU pool vs hosted per-token. Let us know which utilization bands you want emphasized.

Thanks,
Ben
Enterprise Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: quote-Atlas-20270412.pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jocelyn Park <jocelyn@atlasretail.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.g@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment decision matrix + commit ask

Jocelyn / Samir — thanks for the quick responses. To keep momentum for your May 1 shortlist, proposed next steps: 

1) We will finalize and deliver: (a) a 1-page recommended deployment (Dedicated + overflow Hosted) with explicit commit levels and a short-run payback table, (b) a formal quote (DocuSign link below) you can share with procurement. Delivery: EOD Friday.
2) Security will get a redlined SOC2/controls excerpt and a proposed KMS integration plan to security@atlasretail.com by Thursday.
3) If Atlas needs a live proof-of-concept for the flash sale pattern, we can schedule a 2-week pilot on a scoped data subset; procurement/ops sign-off required.

DocuSign quote (preview): https://www.docusign.com/XYZ-Atlas-Quote

Please confirm Samir (procurement) if you want the quote to be structured as a monthly reserved commit or a quarterly invoice schedule. Also confirm preferred PO terms and whether Atlas requires redwood to sign a separate data processing addendum (we can provide a template).

Appreciate the fast turnaround — Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
